recommendation_summary: Right now, move the existing Python export to the always-on Linux machine and run it with a single systemd service and timer, set well before 08:00. Also keep the failure logs and check that a scheduled run puts the report where it belongs. Airflow, Kubernetes, a worker split and a deployment platform are all rejected. Keeping the command runnable on its own is kept as flexibility, and orchestration is left as a possible later step only if a real need appears. The reply does not mention confirming the Python interpreter or file paths on the server.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You need the correct report by 08:00 and something shippable this week; exact start time is flexible.
labels.Deleted: Airflow, Kubernetes, separate workers, and a deployment platform add no needed capability here.
labels.Bottleneck: The laptop is often asleep when the export should run.
labels.Checked myself: No independent checks in this exercise; you report a working three-minute command, no downstream jobs, safe reruns, and an existing always-on Linux machine.

note: All four record lines are specific and come before the recommendation, which is a bounded systemd timer setup that rejects the Airflow/Kubernetes stack by name.
